clues.text: This city stands on the bank of the Potomac River. Maryland wraps it on the north, east, and south.
clues.narrowing: Rules out most places; puts the player on the northeast bank of the Potomac, wrapped by Maryland.

source.quote: The city stands on the northeast bank of the Potomac River, across from the state of Virginia, surrounded by Maryland to its north, east, and south

clues.text: Summers are hot and damp, and heat with damp air brings storms again and again. Winters are chilly, and a big blizzard can strike every few years.
clues.narrowing: Rules out dry summer lands; keeps hot damp summers with storms and chilly winters with blizzards.

source.quote: The combination of heat and humidity in the summer brings very frequent thunderstorms, some of which occasionally produce tornadoes in the area

clues.text: In 1790, a law chose a site by the Potomac for a capital district of its own. In 1800, Congress moved here from Philadelphia and took its seat.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to the district chosen by law in 1790, filled by Congress in 1800.

source.quote: The Residence Act, adopted on July 16, 1790, approved the creation of the capital district along the Potomac River

clues.text: A designer drew this whole capital on paper in 1791 before its streets were built. The White House, home of the president, has stood here since 1800.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: a capital drawn on paper in 1791, with the home of a president from 1800.

source.quote: Designed in 1791 by Pierre Charles L'Enfant, the city is split into quadrants

clues.text: This city is the seat of rule for the United States. The Supreme Court and the main offices of the land are here too.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the seat of the federal government, with the Supreme Court and top departments.

source.quote: As the seat of the U.S. federal government, the city is an important world political capital

reveal.blurb: Leaders chose a fresh home for their young government by the Potomac in 1790, and a designer planned its streets from scratch. Congress moved here in 1800, and the White House became the home of the president. Washington is the capital of the United States.
